record.paper_title: Open problems of the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Are there only finitely many connected bridgeless cubic graphs that do not admit a 2-homogeneous coloring, where a 2-homogeneous coloring is a proper vertex-coloring in which exactly 2 colors appear in the open neighborhood of every vertex?

evidence.quote:
A proper coloring of vertices where in the open neighborhood of every vertex exactly k colors
appear is k-homogeneous coloring [1]. ... Problem 5.2 There is a finite number of connected bridgeless cubic graphs that do not
admit a 2-homogeneous coloring.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A proper vertex-coloring of $G$ is an assignment of colors to vertices such that adjacent vertices receive different colors. For a vertex $v$, the open neighborhood $N(v)$ is the set of vertices adjacent to $v$ (excluding $v$ itself). A proper vertex-coloring of $G$ is called $k$-homogeneous if, for every vertex $v$ of $G$, the number of distinct colors appearing on the vertices of $N(v)$ is exactly $k$.

A graph is cubic if every vertex has degree exactly $3$, and bridgeless if it contains no edge whose removal disconnects the graph.

Decide whether the following statement is true: there exist only finitely many connected bridgeless cubic graphs that do not admit a $2$-homogeneous (proper vertex-)coloring.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem at the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (2024). A web search did not return any published resolution of the finiteness question for bridgeless cubic graphs lacking a 2-homogeneous vertex-coloring; related literature concerns snarks, normal edge-colorings, and Steiner colorings, but does not settle this specific conjecture.

status_evidence.snippet: Bridgeless cubic graphs without a Tait coloring are known as snarks, and there are infinitely many.
status_evidence.claim: Background on bridgeless cubic graphs; no resolution of the 2-homogeneous coloring finiteness question is reported.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses specialized colorings of cubic graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on cubic graph colorings; does not address the 2-homogeneous coloring conjecture.
